scope: Repeatability resolution only: one unchanged product binary, no A/B, no candidate. Measures how far a single variant's per-process reading moves across nine independent processes so that the plan 9.2 (max-min)/median <= 15 percent row can be judged for feasibility at sub-millisecond magnitudes.

instrument.profile: Release, STATIC, candidate ON, normal allocator, metrics/trace OFF

design.order: interleaved: one process per scale in turn, so both scales spread over the same wall-clock window instead of one scale running first
design.affinity: not pinned; matches the 2026-11-01 seek probe runs that produced the 941/1012 us ledger readings

quantities.primary: per-process median of request_to_present_us over all 16 seeks, then (max-min)/median across the nine process medians
quantities.secondary: same but the per-process median uses only the first 3 seeks, matching the archived v4 group shape
quantities.tertiary: per-process maximum of request_to_present_us (the quantity the Seek gate judges), then the same across-process relative range

decision_rule: Declared before measurement. For each scale and quantity: a relative range above 15 percent means the statistic cannot be satisfied by any implementation at that magnitude, and the 9.2 row is recorded as unattainable there rather than as a candidate defect. At or below 15 percent the criterion stays usable at that magnitude. No threshold is changed by this run and no candidate is accepted or rejected by it.
validity: exit code 0, one PD5_SEEK_ID line, exactly 16 PD5_SEEK lines, records equal to the requested scale. Invalid processes are kept and never replaced.
not_claimed: no formal window or nine pairs
no change to the 20 ms Seek gate or its two covered classes
no device, production or stage acceptance
